coverage_notes.note: Section 3 also makes the fallback license nontransferable. Transfer restrictions cannot be represented by the supplied activity enums; this operative restriction remains unrepresented.
The section 3 fallback depends on a legal judgment that some part of the waiver is invalid or ineffective. The supplied text does not establish that this condition has occurred.

Section 4(a) preserves Affirmer-held trademark and patent rights from waiver, abandonment, surrender, or license; CC0 does not grant those rights. The text does not impose a separate activity prohibition on the public concerning those rights.
Section 2 is an Affirmer waiver, not an express license grant. The modeled public permission describes its effect on exercise of the waived rights.
No external legal determinations or operational facts were supplied.

It is subject to the extent permitted by applicable law.

gap_ledger.reason: The fallback grant, sublicensing bar, and Affirmer's conditional restriction on exercising remaining rights or asserting claims are represented by the cited clauses. The distinct nontransferability restriction in section 3 concerns transferring the fallback license, for which no allowed activity provides a faithful representation.
